en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn how to say how often you do things, and how to ask others. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: How often?
steps.text: Some small words tell us **how often** something happens. Let's put them on a line from 100% to 0%.
steps.body: **always** = every time (100%). **usually** = almost every time. **often** = many times. **sometimes** = some times, not many. **never** = not one time (0%). **Never** already means 'not', so don't add don't: `I never eat meat`, not `I don't never eat meat`.

steps.title: On the scale
steps.text: Here are the five words in real sentences, from 100% down to 0%.
steps.body: With he/she/it the verb still has **-s**: Dimas never **drinks**. Only do/does takes the -s away (Dimas doesn't drink); never doesn't.

examples.en: I always get up at five.
Rina usually takes an ojek to the office.
examples.id: Rina biasanya naik ojek ke kantor.

examples.en: My father often reads the newspaper.
Budi sometimes plays futsal after school.
examples.id: Budi kadang-kadang main futsal sepulang sekolah.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Count the days. How often is that?

question.prompt: Lia goes swimming on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. On the other days she doesn't. Complete: Lia ___ goes swimming.
question.explanation: Three days out of seven is not every day and not zero, so: **sometimes**. Always = every day, never = no days.

steps.title: Where does it go?
steps.text: Now the important part: the position of the word in the sentence.
steps.body: Put the frequency word **before the main verb** (the action word): I usually **walk** to school. With **am / is / are**, put it **after**: They are always busy. am/is/are aren't actions, so they work differently. Trick: look for am/is/are first; if there's none, go before the action word. In a do/does question: Do you often cook? Common mistakes: `I go always`, `She always is late`.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Look for am, is or are first.

options: Pak Joko always is tired after work.
Pak Joko is tired always after work.
Pak Joko is always tired after work.
question.explanation: There's no action word here, only **is**, so the frequency word comes **after** it: is always tired. 'always is' is a common mistake.

steps.title: Build a sentence
steps.text: Now a main verb. Where does always go?

question.solution: I always go to work by bus.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya selalu naik bus ke kantor.
question.explanation: There's no am/is/are here, so **always** goes before the action word **go**: I always go to work by bus. Not 'I go always'.

steps.title: Asking How often …?
steps.text: To ask about someone's habits, start with **How often**.
steps.body: **How often + do/does + subject + basic verb** (no -s): How often do you play futsal? How often does she cook? Answer with a frequency word, or with **every day**, **once a week**, **twice a week**, **three times a month**. **once** (1 time) and **twice** (2 times) are special words; from 3 it's *three times*. **a week** = per week. These phrases go at the **end**: I go jogging every day.

steps.title: Build a question
steps.text: Your sister is one person: do or does?

question.solution: How often does your sister call you?
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Seberapa sering kakak perempuanmu meneleponmu?
question.explanation: How often + **does** (your sister = she) + who (your sister) + basic verb: How often does your sister **call** you? No -s on call, because does already shows 'she'.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip these cards to review the words and patterns.

flashcards.front: Fix it: I go always to the gym.
flashcards.back: I always go to the gym.

flashcards.front: Fix it: She always is late.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Adverbs of frequency

rows: I always get up at five.
We often eat at the warung.
How often do you cook? — Twice a week.
tips: Before the main verb: I **always go**. After am/is/are: She **is always** late.
Trick: find **am/is/are** first. If there is one, the word goes after it; if not, before the action word.
**Never** is already negative: I never eat meat (no don't).
Answers: every day, **once** a week, **twice** a week, three times a month.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar cara mengatakan seberapa sering kamu melakukan sesuatu, dan cara menanyakannya ke orang lain. Yuk, langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Seberapa sering?
steps.text: Ada kata-kata kecil yang menyatakan **seberapa sering** sesuatu terjadi. Yuk, kita taruh di garis dari 100% ke 0%.
steps.body: **always** = setiap kali (100%). **usually** = hampir setiap kali. **often** = banyak kali. **sometimes** = beberapa kali, tidak banyak. **never** = tidak sekali pun (0%). **Never** sudah berarti 'tidak', jadi jangan tambahkan don't: `I never eat meat`, bukan `I don't never eat meat`.

steps.title: Di garis frekuensi
steps.text: Ini kelima kata itu dalam kalimat nyata, dari 100% turun ke 0%.
steps.body: Dengan he/she/it kata kerjanya tetap pakai **-s**: Dimas never **drinks**. Yang menghilangkan -s hanya do/does (Dimas doesn't drink); never tidak.

examples.en: I always get up at five.
Rina usually takes an ojek to the office.
examples.id: Rina biasanya naik ojek ke kantor.

examples.en: My father often reads the newspaper.
Budi sometimes plays futsal after school.
examples.id: Budi kadang-kadang main futsal sepulang sekolah.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hitung harinya. Seberapa sering itu?

question.prompt: Lia berenang hari Senin, Rabu dan Jumat. Di hari lain dia tidak berenang. Lengkapi: Lia ___ goes swimming.
question.explanation: Tiga hari dari tujuh bukan setiap hari dan bukan nol, jadi: **sometimes**. Always = setiap hari, never = tidak ada hari sama sekali.

steps.title: Di mana letaknya?
steps.text: Sekarang bagian pentingnya: letak kata itu dalam kalimat.
steps.body: Taruh kata frekuensi **sebelum kata kerja utama** (kata kegiatannya): I usually **walk** to school. Dengan **am / is / are**, taruh **setelah**nya: They are always busy. am/is/are bukan kegiatan, jadi aturannya beda. Trik: cari am/is/are dulu; kalau tidak ada, taruh sebelum kata kegiatannya. Dalam pertanyaan do/does: Do you often cook? Kesalahan yang sering terjadi: `I go always`, `She always is late`.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Cari dulu am, is atau are.

options: Pak Joko always is tired after work.
Pak Joko is tired always after work.
Pak Joko is always tired after work.
question.explanation: Di sini tidak ada kata kegiatan, hanya **is**, jadi kata frekuensi ada **setelah**nya: is always tired. 'always is' adalah kesalahan yang sering terjadi.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Sekarang dengan kata kerja utama. Di mana letak always?

question.solution: I always go to work by bus.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Saya selalu naik bus ke kantor.
question.explanation: Di sini tidak ada am/is/are, jadi **always** ditaruh sebelum kata kegiatan **go**: I always go to work by bus. Bukan 'I go always'.

steps.title: Bertanya How often …?
steps.text: Untuk menanyakan kebiasaan seseorang, mulai dengan **How often**.
steps.body: **How often + do/does + subjek + kata kerja dasar** (tanpa -s): How often do you play futsal? How often does she cook? Jawab dengan kata frekuensi, atau dengan **every day**, **once a week**, **twice a week**, **three times a month**. **once** (1 kali) dan **twice** (2 kali) adalah kata khusus; mulai 3 jadi *three times*. **a week** = per minggu. Frasa ini ada di **akhir** kalimat: I go jogging every day.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaan
steps.text: Kakak perempuanmu satu orang: do atau does?

question.solution: How often does your sister call you?
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Seberapa sering kakak perempuanmu meneleponmu?
question.explanation: How often + **does** (your sister = she) + siapa (your sister) + kata kerja dasar: How often does your sister **call** you? call tanpa -s, karena does sudah menunjukkan 'she'.

steps.title: Ulangan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini untuk mengulang kata dan polanya.

flashcards.front: Perbaiki: I go always to the gym.
